CTGAN is cited only in the reference list, with no evidence it was run or engaged with in the text.

paper-python-package-sampling-copulae-20.summary: This software paper introduces 'clayton', a pure-Python package implementing Archimedean, Elliptical, and Extreme-value copula models with efficient random-vector sampling, benchmarked for performance against existing R copula packages. The paper situates its work relative to prior copula-based tools, noting that Vine copulas have drawn interest in the machine learning community. SDV's vine copula synthesizer (Sun, Cuesta-Infante & Veeramachaneni 2019) is cited and discussed in prose as related work on dependence modeling, but is not implemented or run in clayton.

paper-hybrid-sampling-method-cwgan-2022.summary: This paper proposes a hybrid sampling method for extremely imbalanced backorder prediction that combines Randomized Undersampling with a Conditional Wasserstein GAN (CWGAN) as an oversampling technique, followed by a Random Forest Classifier, evaluated on a Kaggle backorder dataset. In its related-work discussion the authors describe CTGAN's mode-specific normalization (one-hot encodings, softmax with added noise, Gaussian mixture modeling) as prior art that their own CWGAN architecture departs from, but CTGAN itself is not run or benchmarked. CTGAN's mode-specific normalization for tabular data is cited and described only, never executed.
paper-hybrid-sampling-method-cwgan-2022.needs: Full text not obtained; industry classification (manufacturing vs retail_ecommerce for supply-chain backorder prediction) is an inference from the abstract's domain description only.

paper-generative-adversarial-networks-ga.summary: A systematic review surveying the use of GAN-based methods for image augmentation in agricultural applications, covering major GAN architectures and their reported uses across crop, livestock, and plant-disease imaging tasks. The review appears to cite CTGAN as part of its broader survey of GAN variants. CTGAN is only cited, not run or evaluated, within this agricultural imaging survey.
paper-generative-adversarial-networks-ga.needs: Full text, abstract, and citing sentence were not obtained; cannot confirm how or where CTGAN is discussed (likely a passing mention among many GAN variants in a systematic review of image-focused GANs, which primarily targets image data rather than tabular).

paper-netshare-2022.summary: Reformulates packet and flow header generation as a time-series problem rather than a per-epoch tabular one, so that correlations spanning records survive, and adds bitwise IP encoding and parallel fine-tuning for scale. CTGAN is one of the tabular GANs measured against on fidelity and training cost.

paper-predicting-shear-strength-frp-2022.summary: This paper develops a deep learning model to predict the shear strength of FRP-reinforced concrete beams, addressing the scarcity of experimental data in structural engineering by generating synthetic training samples. The metadata indicates the work cites the CTGAN paper, suggesting CTGAN was used to produce the synthetic dataset underlying the deep learning model's training, though the exact mechanism could not be confirmed from the available evidence.
paper-predicting-shear-strength-frp-2022.needs: Full text and abstract were not obtained; cannot confirm whether CTGAN was actually run to generate synthetic training data or merely cited as related work. Title strongly suggests synthetic data generation was central, but this is unverified.

paper-conditional-wasserstein-gan-oversa.summary: This preprint proposes a conditional Wasserstein GAN with an auxiliary classifier loss (cWGAN) for oversampling the minority class in imbalanced tabular classification tasks, evaluated against SMOTE, ADASYN, Borderline-SMOTE and SMOTENC on seven real-world credit-scoring datasets. In its related-work discussion of recent tabular GANs, it describes CTGAN's mode-specific normalization (Gaussian Mixture Model treatment of numerical columns, one-hot encoding with noise for categoricals) as prior art its own architecture departs from, without running the CTGAN library itself. CTGAN's mode-specific normalization approach is discussed and contrasted with, not executed, in the paper's own generator design.

paper-synevarec-framework-evaluating-rec.summary: This paper proposes SynEvaRec, a framework for comparing recommender systems across classes of synthetic user, item, and rating data rather than single fixed datasets, aiming to address privacy, data-insufficiency, and No-Free-Lunch evaluation problems. The framework's synthetic data generation module is built directly on the open-source SDV library, using its GaussianCopula, CTGAN, and CopulaGAN models to generate synthetic user and item attribute vectors, selecting the best generator per dataset via SDV's own detection metrics. SDV's GaussianCopula, CTGAN, and CopulaGAN synthesizers are run as the actual generators producing the synthetic data that the entire empirical evaluation is built on.
paper-synevarec-framework-evaluating-rec.needs: Full text not obtained; cannot confirm whether SDV software is actually used to generate the synthetic data or is only cited as related work.

paper-optimized-training-deep-neural-201.summary: This conference paper presents a pipeline for generating synthetic 3D objects and scenes with a graphics engine, along with automatic labeling and segmentation, to train and test Deep Neural Networks for vision tasks, showing that DNNs trained on such synthetic imagery can match or outperform those trained on real data. The work is unrelated to tabular data synthesis; it cites the original SDV paper only as a generic reference supporting the claim that synthetic data can substitute for real data in model training.
paper-optimized-training-deep-neural-201.needs: Full text not obtained; only abstract and citing sentence available, so cannot confirm whether SDV is discussed further in the body.

paper-causalwrap-2026.summary: Observes that generators trained to match an observational joint distribution can score well on column-wise utility while distorting causal effect estimates, and fits a post-hoc correction module that pulls a trained generator's samples toward a partially known causal structure, evaluated on synthetic structural causal models of three kinds and on a MIMIC-IV intensive-care cohort against an oracle sampler. Two of the three wrapped base generators are SDV, CTGAN and TVAE, each trained in its standard implementation before the wrapper is fitted.

preprint-countsdiff-diffusion-model-natu.summary: CountsDiff is a diffusion-model framework for generative modeling and imputation of count-based (natural-number-valued) data, extending Blackout Diffusion with a survival-probability parameterization, continuous-time training, classifier-free guidance, and non-monotone reverse dynamics. It is validated on image benchmarks (CIFAR-10, CelebA) and on single-cell RNA-seq imputation in fetal and heart cell atlases, where it matches or beats leading imputation methods. The metadata records a citation to the CTGAN paper, but the quoted citing sentences discuss single-cell foundation models and MNAR missingness with no mention of CTGAN, GAN architectures, or any SDV-family tool anywhere in the retrieved full text, suggesting the CTGAN citation link is spurious or lost in extraction rather than a genuine engagement.
preprint-countsdiff-diffusion-model-natu.needs: The attributed CTGAN citation cannot be located or verified in the full text at all; this may be a mis-linked/false-positive citation match (name_collision) rather than a genuine reference. Flagging for manual verification of the actual reference list entry.

preprint-emdt-embedding-diffusion-transf.summary: This preprint proposes EmDT, a diffusion-based generative model that uses UMAP clustering and a Transformer denoising network to synthesize fraudulent credit-card transactions for addressing class imbalance in fraud detection, followed by an XGBoost classifier for downstream classification. The authors benchmark EmDT against SMOTE, TabDDPM, and two SDV-family models, evaluating classification performance, privacy, and correlation preservation. CTGAN and TVAE are run using the official implementations from the SDV GitHub repository as comparison baselines that EmDT is shown to outperform.

preprint-synthetic-longitudinal-tabular-.summary: This preprint proposes eCDF-copula, a statistically grounded method combining empirical CDFs, copula modeling, and multiple imputation to generate synthetic longitudinal tabular health data while preserving within- and between-visit dependence structure. It benchmarks this approach against four established synthetic data methods on two clinical datasets of very different sizes, reporting superior resemblance and utility with comparable privacy. SDV's PAR sequential model and CTGAN are run as two of the baseline generators against which the new method is compared.
preprint-synthetic-longitudinal-tabular-.needs: Full text not obtained; cannot confirm exact experimental setup (e.g., whether SDV's own PAR/CTGAN implementations were used verbatim or reimplemented) or full list of the four benchmark methods.

preprint-understanding-latent-flow-model.summary: This paper presents an empirical study of latent-space flow-matching models for synthetic tabular data, comparing velocity, score, noise, and posterior-matching learning targets under different probability paths and sampling schemes across seven datasets, and distilling practical configuration guidance balancing utility, disclosure risk, and compute budget. It benchmarks its latent flow variants against several standard tabular generators, including CTGAN and TVAE (run via the synthcity implementation), and against TabDDPM and TabSyn. The SDV library is run directly to compute the shape and trend fidelity metrics used throughout the evaluation, while the CTGAN model itself is cited as one of several baseline generative models compared.
preprint-understanding-latent-flow-model.needs: CTGAN/TVAE baselines are explicitly run through the synthcity implementation rather than the sdv-dev package, so the CTGAN integration mechanism for that part is closer to 'inherited' than 'api_user'; only the SDV library's use for shape/trend metrics is unambiguous api_user.

preprint-note-statistically-accurate-tab.summary: This short preprint proposes a probability-driven prompting approach for LLM-based synthetic tabular data generation, in which conditional distributions of categorical variables are explicitly estimated via LLM prompting and sampled to better preserve feature dependencies than autoregressive generation alone. It positions this method against prior approaches including GANs, VAEs, autoregressive tabular models, and copula-based models, and against other LLM-based frameworks like GReaT and EPIC. CTGAN is only listed among prior generative techniques in the introduction and reference list, with no experiment or code run.

preprint-gem-generative-tabular-fitting-.summary: This paper proposes GEM-T, a lightweight maximum-entropy generative model for tabular data that directly fits low-order (pairwise, third-order, etc.) moments among columns instead of relying on deep neural architectures. Across 34 public UCI benchmark datasets it matches or exceeds two deep-learning baselines on 68% of datasets while using orders-of-magnitude fewer parameters. CTGAN is trained end-to-end as one of the two headline competing generators the whole quantitative comparison rests on, and SDV's DCRBaselineProtection function is run directly to score privacy preservation of all three models' synthetic outputs.
preprint-gem-generative-tabular-fitting-.needs: SDV's DCRBaselineProtection is technically an SDMetrics feature; the paper's own wording attributes it to SDV, which is preserved here per the mis-citation rule.

preprint-quantitative-auditing-fairness-.summary: This paper proposes a framework that uses differentially private synthetic data generation to audit AI fairness while protecting sensitive information, testing it on the Adult, COMPAS, and Diabetes datasets by comparing fairness metrics computed on synthetic versus real data. The synthetic data generation method discussed in the body relies on a mutual-information/maximum-spanning-tree technique for preserving attribute correlations under privacy constraints, not on SDV tooling. CTGAN (Xu et al. 2019) appears only in the paper's reference list among other synthetic-data works, with no evidence it was run or engaged with in the text.
preprint-quantitative-auditing-fairness-.needs: No body-text discussion of CTGAN found beyond the bibliography entry; confirm it is not used as a baseline elsewhere in the full text not captured here.

paper-survival-clinical-trial-hivae-2025.summary: Generates synthetic control arms for late-phase oncology and rare-disease trials by learning covariates and the time-to-event endpoint jointly in one latent variational model rather than in the two-stage pipeline the GAN-based survival generators use, so that censoring and small sample sizes are handled inside the generative model instead of by a separate downstream time regressor. TVAE runs inside the comparison: the Surv-VAE arm is the SurvivalGAN pipeline with its GAN covariate module replaced by the tabular variational autoencoder of Xu et al., while CTGAN and TVAE as standalone generators were considered and excluded on the strength of SurvivalGAN's earlier finding that they are less effective for survival modelling.

preprint-when-tables-leak-attacking-2025.summary: This paper introduces LevAtt, a no-box membership inference attack that exploits string-level memorization of numeric digits in LLM-based tabular synthetic data generators, showing severe privacy leakage in models like RealTabFormer and GREaT, and proposes a digit-perturbation defense that trades minimal fidelity/utility loss for reduced leakage. As controls representing conventional (non-LLM) tabular generators, the authors include CT-GAN and TVAE, implemented through the Synthcity library rather than the sdv-dev package, and find these baselines show no leakage under LevAtt since they generate full rows rather than token strings. CTGAN and TVAE, the models introduced in the SDV-family CTGAN paper, are run as control baselines against which the LLM-based attack surface is contrasted.
preprint-when-tables-leak-attacking-2025.needs: CTGAN/TVAE were run via the Synthcity library rather than sdv-dev; the SDV-family paper is cited as the algorithm's origin but the specific package invoked is third-party, so mechanism could arguably be 'inherited' instead of 'baseline_only'.

paper-survival-conditioning-outcomes-202.summary: Generates survival data by turning the usual factorisation around: time-to-event and censoring indicator are sampled first from a Dirichlet process mixture fitted to the observed outcomes, and the covariates are then drawn conditioned on them, which keeps the synthetic risk structure faithful without requiring the generator to model censoring itself. CTGAN and TVAE are two of the conditional generators the framework is instantiated on, adapted so their conditioning input carries the sampled time and event, with CTGAN's generator described in the paper's own notation as the conditional adversarial case.

preprint-silico-generation-synthetic-can.summary: This preprint introduces OncoGAN, a generative AI tool that combines generative adversarial networks and tabular variational autoencoders to produce entirely synthetic cancer genomes -- including somatic point mutations, copy number alterations, and structural variants -- trained on large-scale genomic datasets, aiming to address the scarcity of open, privacy-safe benchmarking data in precision oncology. The work cites the TGAN paper as the basis for its generative modeling approach, and its abstract's mention of 'tabular variational autoencoders' suggests a TVAE-style component within its architecture, though the evidence does not clarify whether the SDV-family library code was run directly or reimplemented by the authors.
preprint-silico-generation-synthetic-can.needs: Full text not obtained; cannot confirm whether OncoGAN runs the sdv-dev TGAN/TVAE library code directly (api_user) or reimplements the architecture independently (port). Abstract's reference to 'tabular variational autoencoders' alongside a citation to the 2018 TGAN paper (rather than the 2019 CTGAN/TVAE paper) may reflect mis-citation typical in this literature.

paper-subpopulation-synthetic-ehr-2023.summary: Identifies the subpopulations on which a mortality-prediction model underperforms, generates synthetic records for each of them separately, and trains a per-subpopulation ensemble on the augmented data, reporting gains over both a real-data-only ensemble and SMOTE on two MIMIC use cases. CTGAN is the generator throughout: one model is trained per underrepresented subpopulation on training-set samples only and then sampled to add between 0 and 1000 percent of that subpopulation's real size.

paper-synthetic-data-real-errors-2023.summary: Warns that conclusions drawn on synthetic data need not transfer to the real data behind it, because a single synthetic dataset hides the generative model's own uncertainty, and proposes publishing a Deep Generative Ensemble instead: several generators fitted to the same real data, so a downstream user can measure how much a finding depends on which model produced the rows. CTGAN is the generator the whole argument is instantiated on, chosen for its widespread use and for the diversity between independently trained instances, run with fixed hyperparameters across every experiment and varied in hidden-layer count for the demonstration that train-on-synthetic conclusions diverge from real ones.

preprint-real-deal-behind-artificial-202.summary: This paper investigates the inferential utility of synthetic tabular data, showing through a simulation study and a case study that naive statistical inference on synthetic data produces unacceptably high false-positive rates, and that standard-error underestimation persists for deep generative models even after a proposed correction factor. It compares two statistical synthesizers (Synthpop, a Bayesian network) against two deep-learning synthesizers, CTGAN and TVAE. The authors state they used the Python package SDV to train their CTGAN and TVAE models, running them as two of several generators whose bias, standard-error behaviour and confidence-interval coverage are benchmarked.

preprint-framework-auditable-synthetic-g.summary: This paper proposes a framework for generating synthetic data that gives data controllers explicit control over which statistical properties are preserved, coupled with an auditing procedure to verify that no additional, unsanctioned information is leaked. The authors apply the framework to real applications including UK census microdata, comparing multiple synthetic data generators on utility and privacy metrics. CTGAN, cited to Xu et al. (2019), is run as one of several benchmark generators (alongside MST, PrivBayes, PATEGAN, and SynthPop) whose synthetic outputs are evaluated for utility and privacy in the case studies.

preprint-global-measure-simultaneously-e.summary: This preprint proposes a new global measure that jointly evaluates data utility and privacy risk in synthetic or de-identified datasets, based on relative distance between synthetic and original data at the dataset level, along with a graphical tool for visualizing the utility-privacy trade-off. Numerical studies on simulated and real datasets are used to show the measure outperforms existing one-sided utility or privacy metrics. The work cites the TGAN paper from the SDV family, but the abstract does not show how or whether TGAN's synthesizer was actually run in the experiments.
preprint-global-measure-simultaneously-e.needs: Full text was not obtained; cannot confirm whether TGAN was actually run to generate synthetic data for the numerical studies or merely cited as related work.

preprint-evaluating-fairness-impact-diff.summary: This paper evaluates four differentially private synthetic data generators—DP-CTGAN, PATE-CTGAN, an ensemble method (QUAIL), and MST—on downstream binary classification tasks, finding that most degrade fairness outcomes by suppressing minority groups, and shows that multi-label undersampling before synthesis can mitigate this. The DP synthesizers were run via the open-source SmartNoise SDK rather than the SDV library itself. CTGAN is cited only as the non-private base model that DP-CTGAN and PATE-CTGAN were built from, not run directly.
preprint-evaluating-fairness-impact-diff.needs: Descendant models (DP-CTGAN, PATE-CTGAN) were run via SmartNoise SDK, not sdv-dev's CTGAN, so CTGAN itself is cited but not executed.

preprint-invertible-tabular-gans-killing.summary: The paper proposes IT-GAN, a generative model for tabular data synthesis that combines adversarial training with an invertible neural network's negative log-density regularization, allowing a trade-off between synthesis quality and privacy protection. It evaluates IT-GAN against several baseline synthesizers (TVAE, TGAN, TableGAN, PrivBN, MedGAN, VeeGAN) on classification, regression, and privacy-attack tasks across multiple real-world datasets. TVAE, from the CTGAN paper, is run as one of several comparison baselines across nearly all experiments, while the original SDV paper is cited only in passing to describe the Gaussian-copula approach to modeling tables.
preprint-invertible-tabular-gans-killing.needs: Unclear whether TVAE was run via the official ctgan/sdv package or the authors' own reimplementation; no import or library statement given.

paper-recsys-simulators-survey-2022.summary: Surveys simulators that stand in for live recommender systems during development, decomposing them into four components — synthetic user and item profiles, a response function, a feedback loop, and an evaluation procedure — and comparing published simulators on which components each supplies and how each handles real-world drift in user behaviour. SDV is cited twice: as the library SynEvaRec calls to build synthetic user and item profiles with Gaussian Copula, CTGAN and CopulaGAN, and as a source of ready-made metrics for judging generated data quality, grouped into statistical, likelihood and detection families; the survey itself runs nothing.

preprint-generative-synthesis-insurance-.summary: This preprint develops a workflow for generating realistic synthetic insurance datasets to address the lack of publicly available data for actuarial research, applying it to general insurance pricing and life insurance shock lapse data with an R interface to promote adoption. The synthesized datasets are evaluated for machine learning efficacy, variable distributions, and model parameter stability. CTGAN, the neural network architecture for tabular data generation from the SDV family, is run as the generator underlying the entire synthesis workflow.
preprint-generative-synthesis-insurance-.needs: Full text not obtained; affiliation of the sole author and whether an R package wraps the actual sdv-dev CTGAN package (vs. a reimplementation) could not be confirmed from the abstract alone.

preprint-sparse-density-trees-lists-2015.summary: This paper introduces sparse tree- and list-based generative density estimation models for binary/categorical data, offering an interpretable, visualizable alternative to high-dimensional histograms, with an application to crime modus-operandi analysis. In comparing their methods against Density Estimation Trees (DET), the authors tried pre-processing categorical data with 'the Synthetic Data Vault algorithm from Patki et al. (2016)' as an alternative to one-hot encoding, but found it decreased log-likelihood performance and abandoned it. The original SDV algorithm is run as a rejected preprocessing baseline in a comparison against a competing density-estimation method.

thesis-anomaly-detection-railway-radio-2.summary: This thesis develops an automated Radio Network Anomaly Detection tool for Wi-Fi planning on the Torino Linea 1 metro line, combining Autoencoder, Gaussian Mixture Model, and Isolation Forest techniques to flag anomalous radio signal behavior. To address the scarcity of anomaly-free data in early design phases, it builds a synthetic data generation pipeline, testing multiple models and finding that a Tabular Variational Autoencoder (TVAE) paired with a rejection sampling strategy guided by a Random Forest discriminator is most effective. SDV's TVAE is run as the core synthetic data generator underpinning the whole anomaly-detection pipeline.
thesis-anomaly-detection-railway-radio-2.needs: Full text not obtained; cannot confirm whether TVAE was run via the sdv/ctgan package or reimplemented, nor institutional affiliation of the author.
